title: Answer requests the way a host simulator does

blocks.text: You cannot certify, or even test, against a live card network every time you change your code. A host simulator stands in for the network: it takes each request your system sends and answers it the way the network would, and designated test card numbers let a test pick the outcome it wants.

Write the answering half of such a simulator (no sockets: the part a request listener would call). `new HostSimulator(approvalCode)` approves every card unless told otherwise, and `declineCard(pan, responseCode)` sets one test card up to be declined with that code.

items: it carries every field of the request, with the MTI turned into the matching response MTI (a `0100` is answered with a `0110`, a `0200` with a `0210`);
an approved request gets response code `00` in field 39 and the approval code in field 38;
a request for a card set up to be declined gets that card's response code in field 39 and no field 38, because nothing was approved.
The request is not changed. Your caller still holds it, for example to match the answer to what it sent.
A message that is already a response (`0110`, `0210`, ...) cannot be answered; refuse it with an `ISOException`.

cases.says: an approved request is answered with a copy of it carrying the response MTI, response code 00 and the approval code
a card set up to be declined gets its response code and no approval code
answering a request does not change the request itself
a message that is already a response is refused with an ISOException
